supplier_excerpts.exact_statement: For physical unit assignments use length coordinates $x^0=ct_{\rm phys}$ and spatial coordinates in metres, where $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. In this convention the metric components, a unit observer $u$, and a length-normalized Killing field $\xi$ are dimensionless. Other coordinate choices transform component units by their coordinate Jacobians. State maps and geometric currents have the types and units in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]: a formal marker density $n$ is $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; entropy density $s$ is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; a $C^1$ entropy current $S^a$ has components $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; and its physical flux is $cS^a$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Its geometric divergence $\nabla_aS^a$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-4}}$, so $c\nabla_aS^a$ is entropy production per physical volume per second. The symmetric stress tensor $\mathsf T^{ab}$ has components in pascals in length coordinates; it is a tensor, not an observer-independent array of energy densities. The state-function energy density $\varepsilon$ and the observer projection $\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b$ remain distinct unless a material model identifies them.

Adopt the selected stationary bath of [[post-tgr-stationary-equilibrium]] on its connected smooth Lorentzian domain. A finite-cell preparation in this item means exactly the setup of [[thm-tgr-finite-cell-gibbs-factorization]]: finitely many $r\ge1$ noninteracting cells with finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces $\mathcal H_i$, Hermitian proper Hamiltonians $H_i$ in joules, and dimensionless Hermitian number matrices $Q_i$ with nonnegative integer eigenvalues and $[H_i,Q_i]=0$. Their tensor product is $\mathcal H=\bigotimes_{i=1}^r\mathcal H_i$; each cell operator acts as the identity on the other factors.

A state $\omega$ is a **$\beta$-KMS state for $\alpha$ in physical time** when for every $A,B\in\mathcal A$ there is a bounded function $F_{A,B}:S_b\to\mathbb C$ (that is, $\sup_{z\in S_b}|F_{A,B}(z)|<\infty$) that is continuous on $S_b$, complex-differentiable at every point of $S_b^\circ$, and satisfies

Let $\mathcal A$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra and let $t\mapsto\alpha_t$ be a strongly continuous one-parameter group of $*$-automorphisms of $\mathcal A$. Let $\omega$ be a $\beta_K$-KMS state for $\alpha$ in the physical-time convention of [[def-qsm-kms-state]], where $\beta_K>0$ has units $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$ and $\hbar>0$ has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$. For a constant dimensionless $\lambda>0$, define
$$\alpha^\lambda_\tau:=\alpha_{\tau/\lambda},$$
where $t$ and $\tau$ are real time parameters in seconds. Then $\omega$ is a $\lambda\beta_K$-KMS state for $\alpha^\lambda$, with strip width $\lambda\beta_K\hbar$ seconds. Conversely, if $\omega$ is a $\widehat\beta$-KMS state for $\alpha^\lambda$, then it is a $(\widehat\beta/\lambda)$-KMS state for $\alpha$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

derivations.claim: By [F1], the full product state is $\beta_K$-KMS for the grand-generator dynamics. The embedded cell algebra $\mathcal A_i$ is invariant under that dynamics: all lifted cell generators commute, and conjugation by the other tensor factors cancels, leaving $\alpha^{K,i}_{t_K}$. Restricting the full-state strip functions to observables in this invariant subalgebra gives the KMS boundary values for $\omega_i$, since the product density restricts to $\rho_i$. Thus $\omega_i$ is $\beta_K$-KMS for $\alpha^{K,i}$.

Since $G_{K,i}=N_iG_i$ and $N_i$ is constant along the selected orbit, $\alpha^{\mathrm{loc},i}_{\tau}=\alpha^{K,i}_{\tau/N_i}$. Apply [F3] with $\lambda=N_i$ to obtain the $N_i\beta_K$-KMS strip and width $\hbar N_i\beta_K$. The stationary normalization in [F3] gives $T_i=T_K/N_i$, so $N_i\beta_K=N_i/(k_BT_K)=1/(k_BT_i)$. If $X\in\mathcal A_i^0$, then conjugation by $e^{i\tau\mu_iQ_i/\hbar}$ fixes $X$, so the local grand and physical $H_i$ automorphisms agree there.

citations.quote: Adopt the selected stationary bath of [[post-tgr-stationary-equilibrium]] on its connected smooth Lorentzian domain. A finite-cell preparation in this item means exactly the setup of [[thm-tgr-finite-cell-gibbs-factorization]]: finitely many $r\ge1$ noninteracting cells with finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces $\mathcal H_i$, Hermitian proper Hamiltonians $H_i$ in joules, and dimensionless Hermitian number matrices $Q_i$ with nonnegative integer eigenvalues and $[H_i,Q_i]=0$. Their tensor product is $\mathcal H=\bigotimes_{i=1}^r\mathcal H_i$; each cell operator acts as the identity on the other factors.

Fix a cell label $i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$ in [[thm-tgr-finite-cell-gibbs-factorization]], let $x_i=\chi(i)$ be its assigned point, and write $N:=N_i=N(x_i)>0$, $H_{\mathrm{loc}}:=H_i$, $Q:=Q_i$, and $\mu_{\mathrm{loc}}:=\mu_i$. Let $\beta_K>0$ in joules$^{-1}$ and $\mu_K$ in joules be the global parameters supplied there. Put $G_{\mathrm{loc}}:=H_{\mathrm{loc}}-\mu_{\mathrm{loc}}Q$ and $G_K:=NG_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Set $\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}:=N\beta_K$ and define the cell normalizer $Z_{\mathrm{loc}}:=Z_i=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H_i}e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}G_{\mathrm{loc}}}=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H_i}e^{-\beta_KG_K}>0$. Let $\sigma$ be the cell Gibbs density supplied by that theorem, so $\sigma=Z_{\mathrm{loc}}^{-1}e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}G_{\mathrm{loc}}}=Z_{\mathrm{loc}}^{-1}e^{-\beta_KG_K}$. For neutral Hermitian matrices, define
$$\alpha^{\mathrm{loc}}_\tau(C):=e^{iG_{\mathrm{loc}}\tau/\hbar}Ce^{-iG_{\mathrm{loc}}\tau/\hbar},\qquad \alpha^K_t(C):=e^{iG_Kt/\hbar}Ce^{-iG_Kt/\hbar}.$$
For this selected cell, let $q$ be the common charge in coulombs and $\Phi_i:=\Phi_\xi(x_i)$ its compensated potential in volts from the supplier. Define $H_{K,i}:=NH_{\mathrm{loc}}+q\Phi_iQ$ in joules, and write $H_K:=H_{K,i}$ in the physical control below. The supplier normalization gives $N\mu_{\mathrm{loc}}+q\Phi_i=\mu_K$, hence $H_K=G_K+\mu_KQ$.

Let $A=A^*$ and $B=B^*$ satisfy $[A,Q]=[B,Q]=0$. Then their local proper-time and Killing-time dynamics agree after $\tau=Nt$.

Let $h:[0,S]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, with $S>0$ seconds, and let $h(\tau)B$ have units joules. For dimensionless $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$, the proper-time grand-generator control $G_{\mathrm{loc}}-\epsilon h(\tau)B$ corresponds in Killing time to $G_K-\epsilon N h(Nt)B$. Define $E_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)$ and $E_K(t)$ as the finite-time expectations of $A$ from the same initial density $\sigma$ under these controls. Because $A$ and $B$ commute with $Q$, replacing each grand generator by its physical Hamiltonian changes the propagator only by a unitary generated by a constant multiple of $Q$ and leaves the expectation of $A$ unchanged. Thus these expectations also equal those obtained from the respective physical controls $H_{\mathrm{loc}}-\epsilon h(\tau)B$ and $H_K-\epsilon Nh(Nt)B$. In particular,
$$E_K(t)=E_{\mathrm{loc}}(Nt)\qquad(0\le t\le S/N).$$
The finite-time Kubo expansions have identical first-order terms under this rescaling and the same quadratic remainder bound. With
$$R_{\mathrm{loc}}(u):=\frac{i}{\hbar}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma[\alpha^{\mathrm{loc}}_u(A),B]\right),\qquad C_S:=\frac{2}{\hbar}\int_0^S|h(s)|\,\|B\|\,ds,$$
the local expansion is
$$E_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma\alpha^{\mathrm{loc}}_\tau(A))+\epsilon\int_0^\tau h(s)R_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau-s)\,ds+r_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau),\qquad |r_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)|\le\|A\|\frac{(|\epsilon|C_S)^2e^{|\epsilon|C_S}}2.$$
Use $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, so $C_S$ is dimensionless and $R_{\mathrm{loc}}$ has units $[A][B]/(\mathrm{J\,s})$. The Killing-time response kernel is $R_K(t)=R_{\mathrm{loc}}(Nt)$ and its control amplitude is $Nh(Nt)$.

For the equilibrium correlation spectral measures, use the Fourier convention of [[thm-qsm-dt-spectral-fdt]]. If $D_N(\omega):=N\omega$, then
$$S_K=(D_N)_*S_{\mathrm{loc}},\qquad S_K(\omega)=N^{-1}S_{\mathrm{loc}}(\omega/N)$$
in distribution notation; the measure form preserves the weights of delta-function spectral lines. Since $\beta_K\hbar(N\omega)=\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\hbar\omega$, detailed balance is unchanged. Any zero-frequency atom remains an atom at zero and is not assigned a value by the coth formula, which remains restricted to nonzero frequencies.

For a static local perturbation $G_{\mathrm{loc}}-\lambda B$, where $\lambda B$ has units joules, the re-prepared Gibbs family satisfies
$$\left.\frac{d}{d\lambda}\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\lambda B)\right|_{\lambda=0}=\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{KM},\sigma}(B,B)=N\beta_K\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{KM},\sigma}(B,B)\ge0.$$
Here $\delta B:=B-\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma B)I$ and
$$\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{KM},\sigma}(B,B):=\int_0^1\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma^{1-u}\delta B\,\sigma^u\delta B\right)\,du.$$
It reduces to the ordinary variance when $B$ commutes with $G_{\mathrm{loc}}$; no such reduction is asserted otherwise. These are exact finite-dimensional deductions for the constructed neutral cell. They imply no infinite-time relaxation, dc transport coefficient, or response law for arbitrary interacting reduced states.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

$$\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{KM},\sigma}(B,B):=\int_0^1\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma^{1-u}\delta B\,\sigma^u\delta B\right)\,du.$$

derivations.claim: The postulated preparation [F1] supplies a finite-dimensional cell density $\sigma$ and $[H_i,Q_i]=0$. The Hamiltonian matrices in the two displayed control equations are continuous and Hermitian on their compact time intervals. For either equation write it as $U'(s)=K(s)U(s)$ with continuous matrix $K$ and $M:=\sup_s\|K(s)\|<\infty$. The ordered-integral series $I+\sum_{n\ge1}\int_{0\le s_n\le\cdots\le s_1\le s}K(s_1)\cdots K(s_n)\,ds_n\cdots ds_1$ converges uniformly, since its $n$th term has norm at most $(Ms)^n/n!$, and solves the integral equation by termwise integration. If $U,V$ were two solutions, their difference $D:=U-V$ would satisfy the homogeneous integral equation; iterating it bounds $\|D(s)\|$ by $\sup_s\|D(s)\|(Ms)^n/n!$ for every $n$, so $D=0$. Differentiating $U^*U$ and using Hermiticity of each controlled Hamiltonian gives $(U^*U)'=0$; the identity initial value therefore makes each solution unitary.

Define $V(t):=e^{-iq\Phi_iQ_it/\hbar}U_{\mathrm{loc}}(N_it)$. Since $[Q_i,H_i]=[Q_i,B]=0$, differentiating and using the chain rule gives $i\hbar V'(t)=[H_{K,i}-\epsilon N_i h(N_it)B]V(t)$, with $V(0)=I_{\mathcal H_i}$. By uniqueness from step 1.1, $V=U_K$. The factor $e^{-iq\Phi_iQ_it/\hbar}$ commutes with $A$, so the trace definition gives $E_K(t)=E_{\mathrm{loc}}(N_it)$.

Retain the inherited smooth-geometry premise [F3] when using the charged-stationarity relation $N_i\mu_i+q\Phi_i=\mu_K$ supplied by the prepared-cell data [F1]. Put $\widehat U_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and $\widehat U_K$ for the propagators of the grand-generator controls stated in [F2]. The identities $H_i=G_i+\mu_iQ_i$ and $H_{K,i}=N_iG_i+\mu_KQ_i$, where $N_i\mu_i+q\Phi_i=\mu_K$, imply $U_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)=e^{-i\mu_iQ_i\tau/\hbar}\widehat U_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)$ and $U_K(t)=e^{-i\mu_KQ_it/\hbar}\widehat U_K(t)$. These relations follow by differentiating each right-hand side and using $[G_i,Q_i]=[B,Q_i]=0$. Since $[A,Q_i]=0$, the trace expectations under the physical and grand-generator propagators agree. Therefore [F2] applies to the explicitly defined expectations.

Apply [F2] to the same fixed initial density for the finite-time response, to its spectral statement for the equilibrium correlations, and to its separately re-prepared Gibbs family for the static derivative. The first preparation remains $\sigma$ throughout the finite-time controls; $\sigma_\lambda$ is a distinct re-preparation, and none of these deductions is an observed measurement or an infinite-time limit.

citations.quote: For physical unit assignments use length coordinates $x^0=ct_{\rm phys}$ and spatial coordinates in metres, where $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. In this convention the metric components, a unit observer $u$, and a length-normalized Killing field $\xi$ are dimensionless. Other coordinate choices transform component units by their coordinate Jacobians. State maps and geometric currents have the types and units in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]: a formal marker density $n$ is $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; entropy density $s$ is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; a $C^1$ entropy current $S^a$ has components $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; and its physical flux is $cS^a$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Its geometric divergence $\nabla_aS^a$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-4}}$, so $c\nabla_aS^a$ is entropy production per physical volume per second. The symmetric stress tensor $\mathsf T^{ab}$ has components in pascals in length coordinates; it is a tensor, not an observer-independent array of energy densities. The state-function energy density $\varepsilon$ and the observer projection $\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b$ remain distinct unless a material model identifies them.

Let $O$ be a connected domain with the stationary Lorentzian data, potential
$A$, field $F=dA$, Killing field $\xi$, lapse $N=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}$, future
unit stationary observer $u=\xi/N$, and charged transport on the future mass
shell from [[def-tgr-charged-liouville-data]]. Let $m>0$, $q\in\mathbb R$,
$\beta:=u/(k_BT)$ for a smooth proper-temperature scalar $T:O\to(0,\infty)$,
and $\zeta:=\mu/(k_BT)$ for a smooth chemical-potential scalar
$\mu:O\to\mathbb R$. Define $f(x,P)=\exp(\zeta+g(\beta,P))$. Without any global
potential-symmetry assumption,
$$\mathcal L_{F,q}f=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \beta\text{ is Killing and }d\zeta=-cq\,\iota_\beta F.$$

Let $r\ge1$ be finite. For each cell $i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$, let $\mathcal H_i$ be a complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d_i\ge1$, let $H_i=H_i^*$ be a Hermitian proper Hamiltonian in joules, and let $Q_i=Q_i^*$ be a dimensionless number observable whose eigenvalues lie in $\mathbb N_0$. Assume $[H_i,Q_i]=0$. Operators $H_i,Q_i$ on the total space $\mathcal H:=\bigotimes_{i=1}^r\mathcal H_i$ mean their lifts acting on the $i$th tensor factor and as the identity on the other factors; no intercell interaction is included.

Fix one cell $i$ of the finite preparation in [[post-tgr-selected-gibbs-kms-preparation]], at its assigned event $p_i\in O$, with $N_i=N_\xi(p_i)$, $T_i=T(p_i)$, and $\mu_i=\mu(p_i)$. Set $\beta_K:=(k_BT_K)^{-1}>0$ in joules$^{-1}$. Let $\mathcal A_i=\mathcal B(\mathcal H_i)$, let $G_i:=H_i-\mu_iQ_i$ be its proper grand generator in joules, let $G_{K,i}:=N_iG_i$ be its Killing-time grand generator, and let $\omega_i(X):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_iX)$. Use length coordinates $x^0=ct$, with $c>0$ the speed of light in metres per second and the reference-normalized $\xi$ dimensionless in these coordinates. Choose an open interval $I_{K,i}\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing $0$ on which the integral curve through $p_i$ remains in $O$. Define the unique smooth curve $\gamma_i:I_{K,i}\to O$ by
$$\gamma_i(0)=p_i,\qquad \frac{d\gamma_i}{dt_K}(t_K)=c\,\xi_{\gamma_i(t_K)},$$
where $t_K$ is physical Killing time in seconds; the equation states its parameterization by the reference-normalized Killing field. This curve is future-directed timelike. The stationary normalization used in [[thm-tgr-kms-orbit-time-rescaling]] gives $\xi(N_\xi)=0$, so $N_\xi(\gamma_i(t_K))=N_i$ throughout this interval. Its proper-time parametrization is
$$\Gamma_i:N_iI_{K,i}\to O,\qquad \Gamma_i(\tau):=\gamma_i(\tau/N_i),$$
which satisfies $g(d\Gamma_i/d\tau,d\Gamma_i/d\tau)=-c^2$. Thus $\tau$ is proper time in seconds and $\tau=N_it_K$ on the geometric orbit. No completeness of $\xi$ is assumed: the geometric curve is defined on its flow interval, while the finite-matrix dynamics below are defined for all real parameters by their generators and use the same constant rescaling.

Define

$$\alpha^{K,i}_{t_K}(X):=e^{it_KG_{K,i}/\hbar}Xe^{-it_KG_{K,i}/\hbar},\qquad \alpha^{\mathrm{loc},i}_{\tau}(X):=e^{i\tau G_i/\hbar}Xe^{-i\tau G_i/\hbar},$$

where both $t_K$ and $\tau$ are measured in seconds, and $N_i>0$ is dimensionless. Write $\mathcal A_i^0:=\{X\in\mathcal A_i:[X,Q_i]=0\}$ for the neutral observable algebra. Then $\omega_i$ is $\beta_K$-KMS for $\alpha^{K,i}$ and is $\beta_{\mathrm{loc},i}$-KMS for $\alpha^{\mathrm{loc},i}$, where

$$\beta_{\mathrm{loc},i}=N_i\beta_K=\frac{1}{k_BT_i},\qquad \hbar\beta_{\mathrm{loc},i}\text{ is the strip width in seconds}.$$

On $\mathcal A_i^0$, the same proper-time automorphism is generated by the physical Hamiltonian $H_i$, because its chemical-potential term commutes with every observable in that subalgebra. Thus the local temperature is $T_i=T_K/N_i$ for this constructed state and selected orbit. The conclusion is only orbitwise; it does not make a position-dependent lapse into one global time-rescaled dynamics.

derivations.claim: The metric is smooth and has signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $x>0$. The coordinate transformation $X=x\cosh(x^0/L)$, $X^0=x\sinh(x^0/L)$ gives $-(dX^0)^2+dX^2=-(x/L)^2(dx^0)^2+dx^2$, so this is the Rindler wedge. The metric coefficients are independent of $x^0$, hence $\xi$ is Killing, and $g(\xi,\xi)=-(x/L)^2<0$ gives $N=x/L$. Moreover $\partial_{x^0}X^0=(x/L)\cosh(x^0/L)>0$, so $\xi$ is future directed.

With $T=T_KL/x$, $u=\xi/N$ gives $\beta=u/(k_BT)=\xi/(k_BT_K)$, a Killing field. By [A3]–[A4], the auxiliary inputs have $F=dA=0$, $\zeta=\mu/(k_BT)=0$, and $q=0$, so $d\zeta=-cq\,\iota_\beta F=0$ in the exact transport formulation. The forward direction of [F2] therefore gives whole-future-shell stationarity and the global compensator condition required by [F3].

At $x_1=L$ and $x_2=2L$, step 1.1 gives $N_1=1$ and $N_2=2$. The adopted field has $T_i=T_K/N_i$, and the two cells satisfy $[H_i,Q_i]=0$, $Q_i=0$, and $\mu_i=q=0$. Thus the finite-cell hypotheses of [F3] hold with $G_K=N_1H_1+N_2H_2=H_1+2H_2$ and $\beta_i=N_i\beta_K$. Applying [F3] gives the positive finite partition sums and the product state in the Example. The construction is conditional on [F5], inherited through [F2].

The eigenvalues of $H_i$ in the displayed basis are $0$ and $\Delta_i$, so their traces are $Z_i=1+e^{-\beta_i\Delta_i}$ and the normalized diagonal densities are exactly the displayed $\rho_i$. Since $\beta_i=N_i\beta_K$, their tensor product equals $e^{-\beta_K(H_1+2H_2)}/(Z_1Z_2)$.

Apply [F4] separately to the two cells. Their Killing-time KMS parameter is $\beta_K$; the constant lapse rescalings give local parameters $N_1\beta_K$ and $N_2\beta_K$, equal to $(k_BT_1)^{-1}$ and $(k_BT_2)^{-1}$. This establishes the stated model prediction only and reports no experiment.
